question.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion with damping. The position of the particle $y(t)$ at time $t$ is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+6{y}^{′}+25y=17\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

Which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for $y(t)?$

I. $y={e}^{-3t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡4t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t$

II. $y=A{e}^{-3t}+B{e}^{4t}+17\operatorname{cos}⁡t+17\operatorname{sin}⁡t$

III. $y=R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
question.worked_solution:
The general solution is the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution:

$$
y(t)={y}_{c}(t)+{y}_{p}(t)
$$

First, we find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(t),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation ${y}^{″}+6{y}^{′}+25y=0.$ Writing down and solving the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +25 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +9)-9+25 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2}+16 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2} & =-16 \\ \lambda +3 & =\pm 4\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-3\pm 4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ can be expressed in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c}(t) & ={e}^{-3t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡4t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4t), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t).$ The particular solution is of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡t+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

By substituting the particular solution into the differential equation and equating coefficients, we find that $\alpha =-\frac{1}{6}$ and $\beta =\frac{2}{3}.$ So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & ={e}^{-3t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡4t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Only I and III match the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
